assertion: The U.S. national median rent edged up by 0.1 percent from a year earlier in October, according to a new report from Realtor.com. Despite the marginal gain, it was the first annual increase since June 2023.
inaccuracy: The article says 'national median rent'; Realtor.com's figure covers studio/1BR/2BR listings in the 50 largest metros. The rise is $1 (0.1%).
independent_value: Realtor.com release: $1,692, +0.1% ($1) YoY, first YoY growth since June 2023, 50 largest metros
searched: Realtor.com October 2026 rental report median asking rent $1,692 first annual increase since June 2023

sources.title: Realtor.com October Rent Report (PR Newswire via Finviz)

assertion: The Nov. 18 report shows that the median asking rent was $1,692 in October, still 4.6 percent, or $82, below the peak reached in the summer of 2022 but 15 percent, or $221, above the pre-pandemic level.
independent_value: Release: -4.6%/$82 vs August 2022 peak; +15%/$221 vs October 2019

assertion: Two-bedroom property rents posted the largest increase, rising by 0.3 percent year-over-year to a median of $1,889. Median one-bedroom rents edged up by 0.1 percent to $1,566. Studio rents declined by 1.2 percent year-over-year to $1,411.
The report noted that the multifamily construction boom during 2021 and 2022 has kept the median asking rent falling for three consecutive years.
inaccuracy: The article dates the boom to 2021 and 2022; the release cites 1.5M units completed 2023-2025 and a rent decline streak since mid-2023.
independent_value: Release: nearly 1.5M units completed 2023-2025; YoY rent declines from mid-2023

assertion: Nationwide, completions have declined by 26 percent year-over-year to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 330,000, while multifamily units under construction were down by 2.7 percent from a year earlier to 674,000. Multi-family construction starts also decreased by 9.2 percent from a year earlier, standing at 403,000.
independent_value: Release Q3 2026: completions 330,000 (-26.0%), under construction 674,000 (-2.7%), starts 403,000 (-9.2%)

assertion: Freddie Mac’s Nov. 19 data show that the average interest rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose to 7.28 percent from 7.11 percent a week earlier, the highest level in four weeks.
inaccuracy: The article says highest in four weeks; 7.28% exceeds the prior three weeks (7.24, 7.18, 7.11) but is below 7.32% on Oct 22, exactly four weeks earlier.
sql: SELECT "date", "value" FROM econ.fred_indicators WHERE series='MORTGAGE30US' AND "date">='2026-10-15' ORDER BY "date"
measure: Freddie Mac 30-year fixed mortgage rate weekly

assertion: A Nov. 18 report from the National Association of Realtors shows that its Pending Home Sales Index fell to 63 in October, 4.7 percent lower than September and 16.7 percent lower than October 2025. This marks the lowest reading since the record began in 2001.
independent_value: NAR: -4.7% m/m, -16.7% y/y; index 63.0 and record low per TheStreet/HousingWire coverage; Epoch Oct 20 article had September at 66
